item.title: Interpret a switch in language class attendance
item.summary: A course organiser explains how a sign-in change affects the claim that attendance improved.
item.transcript_text:
Tutor: The Tuesday group shows higher attendance after we moved to a code on the board. Does that mean the change made people come more often?
Coordinator: Maybe, but the old list often stayed at the door, where late arrivals forgot to sign. The new code stays up all class. More names could just mean we record more of the people who were already there.
Tutor: We have learners without phones.
Coordinator: We still take their names on paper, so that part stays open. Next week, ask an observer to count people once in each class and compare that total with the register.
Tutor: Should I use the new totals in the review?
Coordinator: Use them, but flag the break in how we collected the data.

questions.prompt: Why might the increase be misleading?
options: The new group is meeting on a different day
Late arrivals are no longer allowed in
The attendance method may now capture more people
The register counts tutors as students
questions.explanation: A change in recording can explain higher counts without changing real attendance.

questions.prompt: What could happen under the old system?
options: People could log in after class ended
Late arrivals could miss signing in
Everyone had to bring a phone
Two classes could share one code
questions.explanation: The list at the door was easier for late arrivals to miss.

questions.prompt: How can people without phones still sign in?
options: By having their names written on paper
By borrowing the tutor’s phone
By signing in at home
By sending a message to an observer

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an observer’s count?
options: To determine who arrives first
To collect proof of why each person came
To replace the register indefinitely
To compare an independent headcount with the register
questions.explanation: The team wants an additional measure for checking completeness.

questions.prompt: How should the review present the new totals?
options: Compare them without any comment
Remove all new totals
Use them and explain the change in data collection
Treat them as proof of more attendance
questions.explanation: The coordinator says to flag the break in measurement.

children.segment_text: the old list often stayed at the door
the new code stays up all class
flag the break in how we collected the data
